name: Install OpenStack DevStack
description:
As you know OpenStack Cinder component is for Storage management. We will recap our installation with DevStack.DevStack is a set of scripts which will install all the OpenStack components and prepare them ready for your use.

We need to run below steps to install devstack setup. we covered these steps on OpenStack basics under topic Install and Configure DevStack. You can copy/paste them into right side terminal.

sudo apt-get update 
sudo apt-get -y git
Lets add a new user 
sudo adduser --disabled-password --gecos "" stack 
sudo su <<EOF
echo "stack ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL" >> /etc/sudoers
EOF
Now lets setup devstack repo and launch the installation script. 
sudo su stack <<EOF
cd /home/stack 
git clone https://git.openstack.org/openstack-dev/devstack  -b stable/kilo openstack 
cd /home/stack/openstack/
echo '[[local|localrc]]' >  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo ADMIN_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo MYSQL_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo RABBIT_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo SERVICE_PASSWORD=password >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo SERVICE_TOKEN=tokentoken >>  /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo CINDER_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo GLANCE_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo HORIZON_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo KEYSTONE_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo NEUTRON_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
echo NOVA_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf

EOF

Just one more thing to add on config file before running the script. We need to set HOST_IP. You can fetch it from /root/ directory. Just do
sudo ls /root
52.11.130.199 tmp
the ip-address will be different for you, so update properly and execute the script as user 'stack'. 
echo HOST_IP=52.11.130.199 >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
sudo su stack 
#move to stack home dir and execute script as
cd ~  
/home/stack/openstack/stack.sh
This installation will take around 20 to 30 minutes, Please feel free leave this machine and take a break :)
Do you what tasks the script script.sh will perform?
answer:
1. Downloads OpenStack code from git repo.
2. Install OpenStack components and resolves any dependencies
3. Start OpenStack components/services.

name: Access Dashboard
description:
If everything went well, you see a message like "stack.sh completed in 100 seconds" .
Now you need to access OpenStack Dashboard, horizon. So point your browser to your HOST_IP ipaddress 
 http://HOST_IP
You will see the OpenStack Dashboard Login page, use admin/password to complete login process.

name: Launch an Instance
description:
Today, we will learn about block storage(volumes) code named cinder.
But first we need to launch a instance,after logging into the dashboard, Launch an "Cirros" instance from Compute->Launch Instances set instance name as webminal_instance or any other name you like ;)
Wait for instance state to become running, Click on Instance name which is webminal_instance. Now you will see 4 tabs like Overview Log Console Action Log Click on Console and please login using username/password "cirros/cubswin:)"

name: Instance Storage details
description:
Once the Console, If you perform "df -h" you see around 24mb.
Its too low right,lets say we want to store a 300MB file. How to do that? If its a local desktop/laptop we might have added an external harddrive or memory stick to it.
But here how to add a memory stick? I mean how to expand the storage of this small instance?
This is where volumes are useful. They are like memory stick we can create a new volume and add it to this vm.

name: Cinder Step1: Create New Volume
description: Lets say want to create volume 'v1' of 1GB. Follow "Compute->Volumes->Create Volumes" and set the volume and size.

name: Cinder Step 2: Attach the Volume
description:
Look up! quick, look up on the sky you will see the 1GB volume floating in the cloud :) Now we need to attach or plug this into our 'webminal_instance' VM. We can do this via 'Manage attachments' under 'Actions' tab.

Now you are looking into 'Manage Volumet attachment' popup menu. From the dropdown named 'Attach to instance' select 'cirros' and say 'attach volume'.

name: Cinder Step 3: Verify Volume
description:
We need to see whether cirros has this newly added 1GB. you know the command to verify, right? so login to cirros instance (like the way you ran 'df -h' few minutes back) and check.

sudo fdisk -l

Can you a partition with 1GB? /dev/vdb? Format it as ext3 and mount it
mkfs.ext3 /dev/vdb && mkdir /newvol
mount /dev/vdb /newvol

That's pretty simple - Just play around with 'volumes' to get more familiar. See you in next session.
